rationale: Extends the map into the previously unread A7 client path and records a sourced correlation gap as a Surface rather than a defect. In client/buffer.go, WaitReplies decodes each ProposeReplyTS and forwards its CommandId to RegisterReply, so the reply identity is available, but RegisterReply discards it as an identity and the Loop consumer reads c.Reply purely in arrival order: it advances a counter i per reply and, for the blocking helpers, Write/Read/Scan take whichever reply arrives first (client/buffer.go:68-72, 92-200). The source itself acknowledges the missing check with the comment 'TODO: if the return value != i, something's wrong'. Because the harness only runs tests in the captured window's packages and the map had no client behavior or fact yet, I recorded this as an unclassified sourced Surface with its reason and range instead of inventing an A7 Behavior/Fact or a candidate obligation. No defect is claimed: whether the client contract requires request-to-reply identity, and what the pipelined window does to the pairing, is unread.

feedback.answered: The A7 client path was read far enough to source a concrete correlation gap: reply CommandId is available at WaitReplies but is not used to match a reply to its request, and the Loop/Write/Read helpers advance by arrival order only, with an explicit in-source TODO that the return value is not checked against the request index. This is now recorded as a sourced, unclassified Surface.
remaining: Whether the client contract requires a reply to be attributed to the request that produced it, and whether the pipelined mode (Pipeline with window > 0) can deliver replies out of order in this protocol.
